findings.what: The change alters which executable warden runs on the host to produce the prepared base or layer that every later build environment boots (security_boundary: host-env). os/exec's Windows PATHEXT lookup, which ran <exe>.exe or another extension beside an extension-less dist/warden in its place, is replaced by os.StartProcess of exactly os.Executable(). This is a security-boundary change by GLOBAL-06's definition. The design carries the Security note the rule asks for (posture before and after, SEC-01 cell, TEST-08 case), reviewed at r1 and r2; the TEST-08 unit form is TestStartDetachedRunsNamedFile and its native form is the blocking windows-hyperv step's case 3.
findings.fix: Nothing to change in the code. The human acknowledges at merge with the Security note in the PR body; the blocking f6-validate-windows-hyperv step (cases 1 and 3) is the evidence on the only OS where the fault exists.

suppressions_note: None: no previous report for this feature, no Tier1-Allow trailers on the branch.
back_to_design_note: The diff is the design as approved at 0c1cad5: StartDetached runs os.StartProcess(exe, [exe]+args) with {null, log, log}, os.Environ() and detachedAttr(), releases it, and on a failed start writes '[warden] could not start <exe>: <err>' to the open log and returns the error; os/exec is dropped from detach.go; detachedArgs, detachedAttr, ConfigFile and TestDetachedArgs are unchanged; ensureFreshBase and ensureFreshWindowsLayer print the Note C line on progress on a failed start (qemu also on a TryHostLock error, a held lock still silent) and return nil; the success lines are unchanged; ensureFreshWindowsLayer takes progress and resolveWindowsBaseImage passes os.Stderr (Note B); the seams are unexported package variables (Note A). No path outside the declared areas.
routing: No MUST for wf-implement. F1 (MUST-review) goes to the PR body for the human's acknowledgement at merge (FLOW-08).
follow_ups_note: No behaviour on main found that this diff does not cause and that needs filing. The qemu end-to-end gap is already tracked (detached-prepare-windows-exe-qemu).
informational: GLOBAL-09/10/11: no default, merge or fallback is added beyond those the Defaults and overrides section lists. The null device as stdin and the inherited environment are what exec.Cmd did with nil Stdin and nil Env, so the child's start conditions are unchanged; Decision 1 names both. 'The build goes on' after a failed start is named there as not a fallback (both outcomes continue on the current base, nothing runs in place of the start). The PATHEXT lookup, an unnamed fallback, is removed.

UX-04: both new lines say what failed, the error, and the exact command that refreshes by hand (prepareFix constant for hyperv, prepareFix(ga) for qemu, so neither command is spelled twice). It is a warning on a build that continues, not a returned error, so no FixableError is called for; the min-grace refusal stays the stop.

Hyperv lock errors: prepareRunning (unchanged) treats a TryHostLock error as 'not running' and goes on to start the prepare, so hyperv never dropped a lock error silently the way qemu did; the asymmetry the design handles (qemu only) is the right one. No finding.

Task 7 (no other self-exec through os/exec): os.Executable() call sites outside tests are hostutil.go (lookups beside the executable, ModuleRoot), relayvm/assets.go, vz/driver.go:403 (codesign -d of the path, not an exec of it), container/container.go:763 (reads warden-io beside it), hyperv/service_windows.go (SCM registration) and cmd/warden-io/initialize.go (PATH prepend, its own path); no exec.Command(exe ...) anywhere. Holds as the design says; the PR body should carry this.

TEST-04: the detached-start test spawns a real child and polls its log line to a 30s deadline, failing there, never retrying; the freshness tests use ages 2h old against a 1m refresh age, far from any RoundAge boundary. Deterministic. On Windows the released child may still be exiting when t.TempDir's cleanup deletes the copied 'warden'; testing.removeAll retries Windows-retryable errors for 2s, which covers it. Worth watching in native case 1, not a finding.
ORCH-04: no transient resource is added; the null-device handle is closed by defer either way and the log by StartDetached's defer, as before.
